title: Local version of the Studio
lead: The same Studio on your computer. Projects sync with this server and the PDF is built on your machine.
loading: Loading the server address and version…
loadFailed: Could not load the server address and version. Refresh the page.

why.title: Why

build.title: Build on your computer
build.text: TeX and checks run on your machine, no cloud runners or quotas needed.

offline.title: Work offline
offline.text: Edit and build on the go, changes reach the server once you are back online.

speed.title: Speed
speed.text: No build queue and no network lag, the editor responds instantly.

why.sync: Once connected, the local Studio pushes your edits to this server and pulls others' on its own, and uploads the built PDF to the project so co-authors and reviewers see the latest version.

requirements.title: What you need
requirements.docker: Docker: Docker Desktop on macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Windows 10/11 with WSL 2, Docker Engine on Linux (amd64 or arm64).
requirements.disk: Disk: about 9 GB for the TeX Live image (downloaded once on the first build) plus a few hundred megabytes for the Studio.
requirements.memory: Memory: 2 GB of RAM and 2 cores per build.
requirements.browser: Browser: any modern one, the Studio opens at http://localhost.

install.title: Installation
install.lead: One command in a terminal. This server's address is already filled in: the connect screen opens after installation.

docker.windows: Install Docker Desktop with WSL 2 and start it.
docker.linux: Install Docker Engine and make sure docker info answers without errors.

install.after: The script pulls the image, starts the Studio and opens it in your browser. On first launch it asks for a projects folder and restarts itself, keep the tab open.
install.portHint: If port 17240 is taken, the script picks the next free one and prints it. Enter it here so the buttons below lead to your Studio.
install.pin: Install the same version as the server ({{tag}})
install.manual: Without the script: one docker run command
install.manualAfter: Then open http://localhost:{{port}} and follow the first-run wizard.

connect.title: Connect to this server
connect.lead: Device code sign-in: no password is typed into the local Studio.
connect.disabled: The administrator turned off git on this server, so the local Studio cannot connect. You can still install it to work without the server.
connect.step1: Open the local Studio with the button below (or paste the server address on its "Connect to a server" screen).
connect.step2: Click "Connect": the local Studio shows a code and opens the confirmation page on this server.
connect.step3: Check the code and click "Allow". Done: you can open the server's projects.
connect.manual: The button did not open the Studio? Make sure it is running, check the port above or paste this address by hand.
connect.version: Server version {{version}}. The local Studio compares its version when connecting and warns if they differ.

project.title: This project
project.lead: The local Studio clones the project from this server and turns sync on. If you already have it, it simply opens.

welcome.emptyLocal: Working in a cloud Studio? Connect to it and the server's projects open here.

connectLocal.title: Connect to a Studio server
connectLocal.lead: The server's projects open here, edits stay in sync and the PDF goes to the server after each build.
connectLocal.urlHint: The one open in your browser, for example https://studio.example.org
connectLocal.signedIn: You are already signed in as {{name}}
connectLocal.connectHint: Click to get a code. Confirm it on the server while signed in to your account.

compat.unknown: Could not compare versions ({{local}} and {{server}}). If something goes wrong, install the same version as the server.
